chunks.arabic_text: أَمَالِي الصَّدُوقِ: عَن أَبِيهِ، عَنِ الْحِمْيَرِيِّ، عَن أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَن أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَن مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمْرَانَ، عَنِ الْحَذَّاءِ قَالَ

translations.en: Amali al-Saduq: From his father, from al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from al-Hadhha who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَا زِيَادُ إِياكَ وَالْخِصَامَاتِ فَإِنَّهَا تُورِثُ الشَّكَّ، وَتُحْبِطُ الْعَمَلَ، وَتُرْدِي صَاحِبَهَا، وَعَسَىٰ أَن يَتَكَلَّمَ الرَّجُلُ بِالشَّيْءِ لَا يُغْفَرُ لَهُ …

translations.en: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: O Ziyad – beware of argumentation because it creates doubt, nullifies deeds and degrades its initiator, it may also happen that a man speaks something for which he is never forgiven …

en.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) advises Ziyad to avoid contentious debates (al-khisamat), as they lead to doubt, nullify good deeds, and degrade the person engaging in them. He further warns that a person might speak a word that results in their unforgiveness.
en.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences of engaging in argumentation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
